# #221 — Add recovery WAL for interrupted realtime agent sessions

State: CLOSED
Author: rodaddy
Labels: none

Parent epic: #220

Research receipt: PR #225, `docs/realtime-agent-memory-research.md`.

## Problem

Pure RAM working memory is fast, but if a process dies or an agent/session is
restarted before wrap/compact, useful context can be lost. Pushing every raw
turn into durable memory would contaminate the trusted layer.

## Goal

Create a crash/recovery holding tier for active session traces. It should
preserve enough evidence for a returning agent to review/compact/promote/
relegate after an unexpected stop, without making the raw trace durable known
memory.

## Required Scope

- Local server-side WAL or snapshot for active session traces.
- Tiny DB/index metadata for recovery discovery, not normal searchable memory.
- Recovery statuses:
  - active;
  - wrapped;
  - recovery_pending;
  - reviewed;
  - compacted;
  - discarded;
  - expired.
- Recovery actions:
  - review;
  - use_for_current_session;
  - compact_to_wrap;
  - promote_candidates;
  - discard;
  - defer.
- TTL and cleanup policy.

## Trust Boundary

Recovery evidence is not durable memory, not shared-kb, and not normal recall.
It is only available to matching scope or explicit recovery tooling.

Crash recovery is review, not truth.

## Relationship To Context Pack

`agent_context_pack` should report pending recovery state and may include a
bounded recovery summary only for exact matching scope. It must clearly mark
recovery content as unreviewed/quarantined.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Open Brain can report pending recovery for an exact
  agent/server/channel/thread/session scope.
- Returning agents can use/review recovery without auto-promoting it.
- Successful wrap/compact can purge related recovery data.
- Tests cover restart/recovery state transitions at the contract level.
- Recovery content is excluded from ordinary `search_all`, `brain_answer`, and
  shared-kb.

## First Next Action

Design recovery WAL/index contract for premature session death; keep recovery
evidence out of normal durable recall.
